sample_unit: ChatGPT responses (16 questions x 4 prompt forms)

links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level of ChatGPT patient education responses by prompt form
links.effect: Form 2 (patient-friendly) mean grade level 12.80 ± 3.38; Form 1 14.23 ± 2.34; Form 3 16.73 ± 2.65; Form 4 14.85 ± 2.76; all above typical patient reading level.
links.quote: Form 2 answers had a lower mean grade level (12.80 ± 3.38) than Forms 1 (14.23 ± 2.34), 3 (16.73 ± 2.65), and 4 (14.85 ± 2.76) (p < 0.05).

links.outcome: Whether ChatGPT provided references in atrial fibrillation answers, including when prompted for sources
links.effect: References provided in only 3 (4.7%) of answers; when prompted for sources, only 3 of 16 (18.8%) responses included them.
links.quote: Across all forms, references were provided in only three (4.7%) answers.

unlisted_practices: Prompt engineering (patient-friendly vs physician-level prompts) to adjust response complexity

screen.practice: prompt constraints for reading level (patient-friendly prompt) and reference prompting
screen.reason: Evaluates ChatGPT's responses to atrial fibrillation questions across different prompting strategies (including patient-friendly instructions and requesting references) to assess impact on readability and accuracy.

primary.practice: prompt framing for reading level and references
